From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@jupiter-robotics.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Private fabric cutover: big-packet failures after handoff

Hi Stephanie / Karthik,

We completed the fabric handoff to Redwood Private this morning (per the cutover plan) and we've started seeing intermittent failures for flows with payloads > 1400 bytes. Symptoms: TCP connections from our on-prem app tier to S3-ish endpoints time out mid-transfer (~30-50s), while small control-plane requests succeed. When we force MSS clamp on the client side things improve, but that's not a viable long-term fix.

Attached a short tcpdump from a failing transfer plus the cutover topology diagram.

Quick details:
- Customer: Jupiter Robotics, staging cluster B
- Cutover window: 07:00-08:30 PT (completed 07:22)
- Failure start: ~08:10 PT
- Observed: Path MTU likely mismatch or fragmentation drop; also seeing SNAT churn in our edge logs around the same time.

Can someone from Redwood look into routing/NAT/SG side? We need this to stop for the production cutover next week.

Attachments: topology-diagram.png (220KB), tcpdump-20261215.pcap (1.2MB)

Thanks,
Liam
Head of SRE, Jupiter Robotics

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 09:58:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private fabric cutover: big-packet failures after handoff

Thanks — quick status: I've pulled the SNAT pool changes and there was a late routing tweak to prefer the new fabric egress next-hop at 07:18 (as part of the handoff). No kernel updates on the appliance in the last 30 days.

What I see in the tcpdump: repeated ICMP Fragmentation Needed messages from an intermediate hop, followed by retransmit timeouts on the TCP stream. However, the ICMPs are not consistently returned to the sender — some flows see them, others don't. That points at asymmetric return path or a middlebox dropping fragmented packets.

Immediate actions I recommend:
1) Temporarily clamp MSS at the customer's edge (1400) to avoid fragmentation while we root cause.
2) Increase SNAT ephemeral port pool on the edge gateway temporarily — the customer's logs show NAT churn coincident with failures (likely causing flow rebinds).
3) Ask Equinix NOC to validate that jumbo/MTU settings are preserved across the cross-connect (I suspect one side is still at 1500 but an intermediate switch is dropping fragments).

I'll prepare a packet-level timeline and propose a playbook for PROD cutover.

-karthik
Principal Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 17:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private fabric cutover: big-packet failures after handoff

Update and proposed mitigations (actionable):

Summary of findings so far:
- Packet analysis (Karthik) confirms "Fragmentation Needed" ICMPs from midpath but inconsistent delivery to sender — symptomatic of asymmetric return path or an ACL dropping ICMP types.
- Customer edge shows bursts of SNAT rebinds correlated with TCP stalls; ephemeral port pool exhaustion is possible under current config.
- Equinix validated their cross-connect preserves 9000 MTU on both ends; they reported a mis-set MTU on a customer-provisioned switch (Jupiter device) which was toggled during the cutover window.

Temporary mitigation we applied (effective immediately):
1) Increased SNAT ephemeral port range for Jupiter's tenant on the edge gateway (to reduce rebinds).
2) Enabled an egress TCP MSS clamp on the Redwood edge (1400) as a short-lived safety-net for the production cutover next week. This is a reversible infra change and will be removed after we confirm path MTU end-to-end.
3) Opened a ticket with Equinix (EQX-4592) and requested the customer's ops confirm the switch MTU is set to 9000.

Next steps and owner assignment:
- Karthik: build a postmortem packet timeline and include a recommended long-term config (DNAT/SNAT tuning, ICMP passthrough policy). Due: Thu 12/17 EOD.
- Neha: verify firewall/Security Group rules for the tenant to ensure ICMP Type 3 code 4 is allowed return. Due: Thu 12/17 12:00 PT.
- Stephanie: coordinate with Jupiter for a controlled re-test during the maintenance window on Friday.

If the customer approves, we'll keep the MSS clamp active only during the Friday window and do an iterative rollback. Priya/Liam — please confirm if a temporary clamp from our side is acceptable for the Friday cutover.

—Vanessa
Sr. Product Ops, Private Deployments — Redwood Inference
